rationale: Stage 1 evaluation for scope GEO-AGENCY-01 (independent SEO agencies with 2–20 staff serving SMB clients on recurring retainers) yields INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE to authorize Stage 2 prospect mining. While the core workflow and recurrence are verified across four independent agency case profiles (What IF Web, SORN.AI, Butter Marketing, Embarque) and reachability is supported via Clutch directory filters (G2 PASS, G5 PASS), evidence for the primary commercial gates remains sparse and below required thresholds. Specifically, only 5 independent verified concrete pain signals were identified against the canonical threshold of 20 (G1 UNKNOWN), revealed willingness-to-pay includes only 4 independent verified signals against the threshold of 5 (G3 UNKNOWN), and repeatable solution gap signals stand at 5 against the threshold of 10 (G4 UNKNOWN). Furthermore, severe commercial and technical threats remain unresolved (G6 UNKNOWN): low-cost bundled SEO suite incumbents (SE Ranking at €109–€235/mo with white-label agency packs; Semrush at $199–$299/mo) and specialized trackers (Otterly.ai, Peec AI) crowd the market, while practitioner evidence highlights strong agency resistance to separate recurring monitoring line items, high churn due to a missing remedial action bridge, heavy sampling costs (requiring n=7 repeats per query to manage stochastic variance), and OpenAI Terms of Use prohibiting consumer UI scraping. Because thresholds are unmet without complete market falsification, Stage 2 customer interviews are not authorized.

scope_integrity_notes: All counted evidence in G1-G5 strictly complies with scope GEO-AGENCY-01 as verified in scope-map.json. Out of 86 raw records, 78 were VERIFIED by Evidence Auditor, but only 22 records map to GEO-AGENCY-01 across 13 unique independence keys. Broad practitioner comments on r/SEO, solo consultants, and unverified company sizes were strictly classified as UNKNOWN scope and excluded from G1-G5 counts, preventing artificial inflation. No evidence was pooled from enterprise buyers or non-agency segments.

strongest_positive_evidence.finding: SORN.AI verified on official website as an independent 2-10 employee boutique agency providing weekly AI visibility reports using Brand Visibility Index quadrant charts.
What IF Web verified as an independent 3-5 employee digital studio in New Zealand managing recurring client citability reporting across AI engines.
Butter Marketing verified on Clutch as a 2-9 employee London agency allocating 70% of its business to GEO and selling standalone $399/mo retainers.
Clutch directory provides a proven, scalable discovery channel with precise filters for 2-9 and 10-49 employee agencies specializing in SEO and GEO.

strongest_negative_evidence.finding: Agency strategist warns against separate recurring AI optimization line items because proving ROI without reliable tracking is a 'losing game', recommending low-lift quarterly audits instead.
Agency owner explicitly labels standalone GEO monitoring retainers as 'snake oil' and bundles AI checks directly into existing SEO retainers without charging dedicated fees.
SE Ranking bundles 100-250 daily AI search prompts across 10-30 projects for €109-€235/mo with an Agency Pack add-on (€59/mo) providing full white-labeling and unlimited scheduled reports.
Academic and empirical research (ARTIFEX) proves single prompt checks carry ±0.37 standard error and 10%-34% variance, requiring n=7 repeated queries per prompt to achieve statistical validity.

Official search-grounded API calls cost $10-$25/1k calls (OpenAI) and $14-$35/1k calls (Gemini), resulting in $14-$35 direct supplier cost per client audit and destroying unit economics at $100/mo ARPU.
OpenAI Terms of Use explicitly prohibit programmatic output extraction and circumventing safety/rate limits, making consumer UI scraping legally and technically unsustainable.

top_unknowns: Viability of authorized data pipeline: can an accurate measurement service be operated economically using official APIs without violating OpenAI/Google Terms of Use?
Unit economics under required sampling: can a $100/mo multi-client SaaS remain profitable when n=7 repeated queries are required to manage stochastic variance?
Agency buyer willingness to pay: will small agencies pay a standalone $100/mo subscription when clients pay $399-$699/mo retainers and bundled SEO suites offer included tracking?
Decision value of ongoing monitoring: do SMB clients actually retain agencies for monthly visibility tracking, or does churn spike when visibility changes cannot be remediated?
